title: His10-MBP-Cas9 Purification
author: Audrey Lapinaite
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ssseeee

steps.title: Harvest cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin down large‑scale overnight cultures in 1 L centrifuge bottles for 20 min at 4000 rpm (or max 3400 rpm if using the lower‑speed centrifuge) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and freeze pellet
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant and either freeze the cell pellet in the centrifuge bottle at –80 °C until purification or proceed directly to resuspension; avoid leaving pellets in the bottles for extended periods.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Add 10–15 mL lysis buffer per 1 L of culture (scale proportionally), vortex to resuspend; optionally transfer to 50 mL Falcon tubes, flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C, retaining 20 µL for SDS‑PAGE analysis.

steps.title: Lyse cells by sonication
steps.instruction: Sonicate the suspension in non‑glass vessels (50 mL Falcon tubes, Oakridge tubes, or plastic beakers) on ice using power setting 6.0: 10 s on, 20 s off, repeat for a total of 5 min. Use a sharp tip for <2 L cultures, blunt tip for >2 L; wash tip in H₂O and EtOH and dry with a Kimwipe before use.

steps.title: Clarify lysate and equilibrate Ni‑NTA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 15,000 rpm for 30 min at 4 °C. While spinning, equilibrate Ni‑NTA resin: transfer ~5 mL resin (for 2–4 L culture) into a 50 mL Falcon tube, add milli‑Q H₂O to ~50 mL mark, invert to resuspend, centrifuge at 2400 rpm for 3 min, discard supernatant; repeat the water wash 2–3 times, then repeat 2–3 times with wash buffer. Use 10 mL of the 50 % (v/v) EtOH‑suspended Ni‑NTA stock to obtain 5 mL resin. Balance all tubes to within ±0.01 g on a digital balance and avoid disturbing the fragile resin pellet when pouring off supernatant.

steps.title: Save lysate sample
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, remove 20 µL of clarified lysate and set aside for SDS‑PAGE analysis.

steps.title: Bind lysate to Ni‑NTA resin
steps.instruction: Decant or pipette the entire supernatant onto the equilibrated Ni‑NTA resin; if the volume exceeds one Falcon tube, split evenly among multiple tubes, mixing resin and lysate gently and avoiding disturbance of the cell‑debris pellet.

steps.title: Rock resin‑lysate mixture
steps.instruction: Incubate the resin‑lysate mixture at 4 °C on a rocker for 30–60 min.

steps.title: Transfer to column and collect flow‑through
steps.instruction: Pour the resin‑lysate slurry into a disposable plastic (or pre‑washed glass) column; collect 20 µL of the flow‑through for SDS‑PAGE and discard the remainder. Optionally monitor fractions with a Bradford assay.

steps.title: Wash resin – first wash
steps.instruction: Wash the column with 5 column volumes of wash buffer, collecting 20 µL of the wash for SDS‑PAGE and discarding the rest.

steps.title: Repeat washes (total five)
steps.instruction: Repeat the 5 CV wash step four additional times (total five washes), each time saving 20 µL for SDS‑PAGE and discarding the remaining wash.

steps.title: Elute protein from resin
steps.instruction: Add 1 column volume of elution buffer to the column five times, collecting each eluate in a separate 15 mL Falcon tube; save 20 µL of each fraction for SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Analyze and pool elution fractions
steps.instruction: Assess each elution fraction by Bradford assay; pool fractions containing protein, measure absorbance at 280 nm, record volume and yield, and print the absorbance spectrum for purity assessment.

steps.title: TEV cleavage of His‑MBP tag
steps.instruction: If desired, add TEV protease (0.5 mg per 250 µL tube) to the pooled eluate at 1 tube per 10–20 mg protein.

steps.title: Dialyze TEV‑cleaved sample
steps.instruction: Dialyze the TEV‑treated sample overnight against Wash Buffer using a Slidealyzer cassette (MWCO 10 kDa or 30 kDa) pre‑chilled to 4 °C.

steps.title: Remove His‑TEV by re‑binding
steps.instruction: Equilibrate fresh Ni‑NTA resin in Wash Buffer (>10 column volumes), pass the dialyzed sample through the resin, collect the flow‑through, then add 1 column volume of wash buffer and collect again.

steps.title: Dialyze into IEX buffer
steps.instruction: Place the TEV‑cleaved Cas9 into a Slidealyzer cassette and dialyze into IEX Buffer A for 2–4 h at 4 °C; avoid longer dialysis to prevent precipitation at low salt.

steps.title: Ion‑exchange chromatography
steps.instruction: Load the sample onto a HiTrap HP SP column; elute with a linear gradient of 0–100 % Buffer B over 20 column volumes, collecting fractions. Cas9 elutes at ~26 % Buffer B. Concentrate pooled fractions to <2 mL.

steps.title: Gel‑filtration polishing
steps.instruction: Apply the concentrated protein to a Superdex 200 16/60 column, collect the appropriate peak, concentrate as needed, and snap‑freeze aliquots.

steps.title: Store purified Cas9
steps.instruction: Store the final Cas9 preparation at –80 °C (snap‑frozen) until use.
